claims.claim: Henrik Williams argued Andersson's 'Min dyrgrip' for 'precious' is lexically correct but loses the corrupting allure that Ohlmarks's 'älskade' caught.
claims.source: Översättning av Sagan om ringen till svenska (sv.wikipedia)

claims.claim: Petter Lindgren expressed nostalgia for Ohlmarks's almost comically elaborate phrasing against Andersson's terse rendering.
claims.source: Översättning av Sagan om ringen till svenska (sv.wikipedia)

claims.claim: Stefan Spjuth found 'Möcklegräva' for Michel Delving sounded like a place from Swedish MAD magazine.
claims.source: Översättning av Sagan om ringen till svenska (sv.wikipedia)

claims.claim: Strömbom found the narrator's voice completely changed in the new translation, so that it was practically a question of two different works.
claims.source: Charlotte Strömbom, 'God åkermark eller fet och fruktbar mylla?' (Vetsaga)
claims.quote: praktiskt taget var fråga om två olika verk

claims.claim: In the prologue's first sentence Tolkien and Andersson use simple language while Ohlmarks does not, turning 'a little' into 'en någorlunda klar bild av' against Andersson's 'litet'.
claims.source: Charlotte Strömbom, 'God åkermark eller fet och fruktbar mylla?' (Vetsaga)

claims.claim: Ohlmarks's sentences are as a rule longer and more complex than the original's, with a somewhat higher stylistic value where Tolkien's word choice is simple and open.
claims.source: Charlotte Strömbom, 'God åkermark eller fet och fruktbar mylla?' (Vetsaga)

claims.claim: Ohlmarks turns 'the pale king' into 'den dödsbleke konungen' and 'bathed Frodo's shoulder' into a bathing 'med dekokten', consistently seeking more drama than the original.
claims.source: Charlotte Strömbom, 'God åkermark eller fet och fruktbar mylla?' (Vetsaga)

claims.claim: In 'Flight to the Ford' Ohlmarks's 'tröttnade aldrig på att inskärpa vikten av' adds a frenzy absent from Tolkien's and Andersson's matter-of-fact statements.
claims.source: Charlotte Strömbom, 'God åkermark eller fet och fruktbar mylla?' (Vetsaga)
claims.quote: tröttnade aldrig på att inskärpa vikten av

claims.claim: Strömbom suggests Andersson sometimes cultivates a style even somewhat simpler than Tolkien's.
claims.source: Charlotte Strömbom, 'God åkermark eller fet och fruktbar mylla?' (Vetsaga)

claims.claim: The Tolkiens Arda reviewer holds that ornate language gets in the way of the story and that Andersson is more faithful to the English original than Ohlmarks, who added editorial glosses such as 'originell lustigkurre' at Bilbo's party.
Andersson said the heroic register, especially in Book V, was the hardest to translate, and that names allow no room to manoeuvre.
claims.source: Intervju: Erik Andersson — om Ringens brödraskap (Tolkiens Arda)
claims.quote: Det finns inget svängrum i ett namn

claims.claim: Andersson observed the book starts out as a children's book and moves into a more sinister mode, and that Aragorn's speech varies between ranger and king.
claims.quote: starts out as a children's book

claims.claim: Andersson called Ohlmarks's version excellent as a creation in its own right even if it does not always follow Tolkien.
claims.quote: As a creation in its own right it is excellent

claims.claim: The Tolkien på svenska essay charges that Andersson tones down the differences between the original's varieties of language, removes Sam's courteous address, lacks the ear for poetry, and that his small deviations all run in the same direction.
claims.source: Om Erik Anderssons översättning (Tolkien på svenska)

claims.claim: The same essay insists that in Tolkien's text how something is said matters as much as what is said.
claims.source: Om Erik Anderssons översättning (Tolkien på svenska)

verdicts.trueWording: Williams calls 'Min dyrgrip' the single greatest translation blunder
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'lexically correct' — Williams says the dictionary rendering is 'min alskling'/'min skatt' and calls Andersson's 'Min dyrgrip' "den allra storsta oversattningsgrodan"
verdicts.note: sv.wikipedia raw HTML fetched. Quote 'Min dyrgrip' appears verbatim in the blockquoted Williams (DN) passage. The corrupting-allure limb is supported in substance: 'Ohlmarks valde ”alskade” vilket visar att han forstod Gollums forhallande till guldsmycket' and the dictionary rendering is 'sann mot Tolkiens genomgaende avsikt att framstalla hur karleken till jordiska ting och jordisk makt binder sjalen och leder till dess undergang'. But the page frames Andersson's choice as a blunder, not as lexically correct.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'almost comically elaborate' — Lindgren wrote 'nastan rart omstandliga' (almost endearingly long-winded); 'komiska bitoner' on the same page belongs to Spjuth, not Lindgren
verdicts.note: Nostalgia and the terse contrast are supported: 'jag har svart att separera fran Ohlmarks nastan rart omstandliga svenska', framed by 'Flera jamforde Ohlmarks ordrika text med Anderssons mer korthuggna', and closing 'Visst blir man mer partysugen av Ohlmarks version.' Attribution to Petter Lindgren (Aftonbladet) is explicit. No quote field supplied.

verdicts.trueWording: later som en ort hamtat ur svenska MAD
verdicts.note: Page: 'I Svenska Dagbladet anmarkte Stefan Spjuth pa oversattningen av namn: ... Fylkes huvudstad, i originalet ”Michel Delving”, kallar Andersson for Mocklegrava, vilket later som en ort hamtat ur svenska MAD.' Every limb supported. No quote field supplied, hence SUBSTANCE. Minor: the body says 'Stefan Spjuth' (as the claim does) while the reference list spells him 'Spjuth, Staffan'.

verdicts.trueWording: praktiskt taget var fraga om tva olika verk
verdicts.note: vetsaga.se/?p=50 fetched raw (TLS verification had to be relaxed; page bytes are double-encoded UTF-8, repaired before matching). Stroembom (bylined author): 'Min upplevelse var dock att berattarens rost var fullstandigt forandrad i den nya utgavan, och att det praktiskt taget var fraga om tva olika verk.' Quote verbatim; both limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: Bade Tolkien och Andersson anvander sig av ett enkelt sprak, men det gor inte Ohlmarks
verdicts.note: Quote 'en nagorlunda klar bild av' verbatim, twice. Directly after the three prologue-first-sentence quotations the essay writes the simple-language sentence; the next paragraph gives the exact comparison: 'Jamfor exempelvis ”a little” med ”en nagorlunda klar bild av”, och vidare med Anderssons ordagranna losning ”litet”.' The passage is identified elsewhere as 'prologens forsta mening'.

verdicts.trueWording: Hans meningar ar i regel langre och mer komplicerade i sin uppbyggnad an originalets
verdicts.note: Quote 'nagot hogre stilvalor' verbatim: 'Medan Tolkiens ordval ofta ar av en enkel och oppen karaktar tycks Ohlmarks ha en forkarlek for begrepp som ringar in och avgransar och har en nagot hogre stilvalor.' Both limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: Ohlmarks ordval tycks genomgaende strava efter en hogre dramatik
verdicts.note: Quote 'den dodsbleke konungen' verbatim. Page: 'Sa blir exempelvis ”bathed Frodo’s shoulder” i Ohlmarks oversattning ”baddade Frodos skuldra med dekokten”, medan Andersson ratt och slatt skriver: ”baddade Frodos axel”. En annan liten men typisk Ohlmarksforstarkning ar oversattningen av ”the pale king” med ”den dodsbleke konungen”.' Drama limb: 'strava efter att uppna en hogre grad av dramatik an originalet'.

verdicts.trueWording: uttrycker Ohlmarks mening aven en frenesi som inte aterfinns hos Tolkiens eller Anderssons relativt sakliga yttranden
verdicts.note: Quote 'trottnade aldrig pa att inskarpa vikten av' verbatim, in the passage explicitly introduced as 'kapitel XII, eller ”Flight to the Ford”'. All limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: Andersson ibland odlar en stil som ar annu nagot enklare an Tolkiens
verdicts.note: Quote 'annu nagot enklare an Tolkiens' appears verbatim: 'Man skulle mojligen kunna havda att Andersson ibland odlar en stil som ar annu nagot enklare an Tolkiens, men detta aterkommer jag till senare.' Restated later as 'Jag tycker mig ana att Andersson ibland odlar en annu enklare stil an Tolkien'. Hedged ('man skulle mojligen kunna havda'), which the claim's 'suggests' matches.

verdicts.trueWording: ett svulstigt sprak som svaller over stor berattelsen
verdicts.note: tolkiensarda.se art31_2 (review by Patrik Centerwall) fetched raw, decoded iso-8859-1. Quote 'originell lustigkurre' verbatim, in Ohlmarks's rendering of Bilbo's birthday speech ('ja-rop -- och ett enstaka nej av nagon originell lustigkurre'), presented as one of Ohlmarks's 'egna, vidlyftiga tolkningar'. Faithfulness limb: 'Andersson pa manga olika satt ar trognare det engelska originalet an Ohlmarks'. Ornate-language limb: the svulstigt sentence above.

verdicts.trueWording: Den heroiska stilen, sarskilt i bok V, har varit extremt svar
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'the hardest to translate' — asked for the hardest task so far, Andersson answered 'namnen', not the heroic register, which he called only 'extremt svar'
verdicts.note: tolkiensarda.se art28_1 fetched raw. Quote 'Det finns inget svangrum i ett namn' verbatim, and it is his answer to 'Vad har varit den svaraste oversattningsuppgiften hittills? — Dar maste jag anda svara: namnen.' The heroic-style sentence answers a separate question about what is difficult.

verdicts.trueWording: Sometimes the language he uses gives a glimpse of his identity as the great king Aragorn
verdicts.note: theonering.net page fetched raw. Quote verbatim: 'It starts out as a children’s book, as a continuation of “Bilbo”, with a Birthday party. Then the story progresses into a more sinister mode.' Register limb supported: 'Take the Vidstige (Strider/ P.) character, for instance, he changes all the time. Sometimes the language he uses gives a glimpse of his identity as the great king Aragorn.' The page says Strider/Vidstige, never the word 'ranger'; the page is TORn's fan translation of a Svenska Dagbladet article, not a TORn-conducted interview.

verdicts.trueWording: As a creation in its own right it is excellent, even if it does not always follow Tolkien
verdicts.note: Same page, verbatim: '– As a creation in its own right it is excellent, even if it does not always follow Tolkien; you have to be modest when you criticise careless mistakes and such.' Attributed to Erik Andersson.

verdicts.trueWording: dessa sma andringar, alla i samma riktning, upprepas gang efter gang
verdicts.note: tolkien.mbor.se/omandersson.php fetched raw. Quote 'alla i samma riktning' verbatim. All four limbs on the page: 'att tona ner skillnaderna mellan originalets olika sprakbruk'; 'Dessutom har Andersson har trollat bort det hovliga tilltalet Mr. Pippin' in Sam's line (the essay explains Sam is Frodo's servant and lower in rank); 'Kort sagt kravs det ett ora for poesin i Tolkiens sprak. Andersson hade inte det orat.'

verdicts.trueWording: lika viktigt hur nagot sags som sjalva handlingen
verdicts.note: Same page: 'I Tolkiens text ar det lika viktigt hur nagot sags som sjalva handlingen.' The comparand on the page is the plot/action itself rather than 'what is said'; the claim's substance (manner weighs as much as content) holds. No quote field supplied.
